quizzes.title: Getting Started Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: Introduction to Python, Variables, Types & Input, Operators & Conditions.

questions.prompt: How does Python group the lines inside an if statement?
questions.explanation: Python uses indentation (usually 4 spaces) instead of braces. The wrong indentation is a syntax error.
5 is an int, 5.0 is a float and "5" in quotes is a str. print shows the full class names.
// is floor division (3), % is the remainder (1) and ** is the power (8).
An f-string evaluates whatever is inside { }: upper() gives SARA and len gives 4.

questions.prompt: What type does input() always return?
options: It depends on what the user types
questions.explanation: input() always gives text. Convert it with int() or float() when you need a number.

questions.prompt: Complete the condition so that a person who is exactly 18 counts as an adult.
questions.explanation: >= means "greater than or equal to", so 18 passes. A plain > would not.

quizzes.title: Data & Control Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: Loops, Lists & Tuples, Dictionaries & Sets, Functions.

questions.explanation: range(start, stop, step) stops before stop. 2, 4, 6 are printed and 8 is not reached.
questions.code:
for i in range(2, 8, 2):
    print(i, end=" ")

questions.explanation: A slice [1:3] takes indexes 1 and 2 (the end is excluded). Index -1 is the last item.
get() returns the default (0) for a missing key instead of an error. The dict has 2 keys by then.
f(5) uses the default y=10, so 15. f(5, y=1) uses y=1, so 6.

questions.prompt: Which of these cannot be changed after it is created?
questions.explanation: Tuples are immutable. Lists, dictionaries and sets can be changed.

questions.prompt: Complete the code so it prints the squares of 1, 2 and 3.
questions.code:
squares = [n * n for n in ____(1, 4)]
print(squares)
questions.explanation: range(1, 4) gives 1, 2, 3. The comprehension squares each number.
__init__ stored "Rex" in self.name, and speak() uses it.
int("abc") raises ValueError, so the except block runs. finally always runs afterwards.

questions.prompt: What does "with open(...) as f:" do for you?
options: Opens the file in a new window
Closes the file automatically, even if an error happens
Creates a copy of the file
questions.explanation: The with statement guarantees the file is closed when the block ends.
B overrides hi() but calls the parent's version with super(), so "B" + "A".

questions.prompt: Which file mode erases the old content before writing?
questions.explanation: "w" opens for writing and truncates the file. "a" appends and "r" only reads.

questions.prompt: Complete the keyword that signals an error.
questions.explanation: raise throws an exception that the except block can catch.
